title: Hold a nail upright while another robot arm hammers it in
instruction: Stand the nail's point in the hole in the wooden post and hold it upright while the other robot arm hammers it in; let go once it stands by itself and keep clear of the hammer.
context: A helper who holds a part for someone else's tool has to hold it well, then get out of the way at the right moment. This checks both: a nail that falls cannot be driven, and a hand left in the way is hit.
setup: A 90 x 90 cm wooden table top, 75 cm high. Two YAM arms stand side by side at the back edge, 50 cm apart; the controlled arm is the right one in the screenshot. Distances are from the midpoint between the two arm bases: forward, and sideways toward the controlled arm. A wooden post, 10 x 10 cm and 6 cm tall, centred 34 cm forward on the centre line, with a square hole 9.2 mm wide down the middle of its top. A steel nail, 10 cm long, 8 mm diameter with a rounded point and a 22 mm head, 80 g, lies across a small wooden rack (two blocks 3 cm wide and 2 cm high) 26 cm forward and 14 cm toward the controlled arm, pointing sideways with its head toward the middle. A small hammer, 130 g in all: a 26 cm wooden handle with a flat-sided rubber grip, 20 x 24 mm, and a 2 x 2 x 7 cm steel head. It stands on its face 24 cm forward and 21 cm toward the other arm, head toward the middle, the handle level with its end on a wooden rest block. The other arm waits until the nail stands in the hole, takes the hammer, gives light taps while a hand is near the nail and full blows once the hand is 12 cm away, then puts the hammer back. It does the same in every trial.
scoring: The distance the nail went into the post, over 4 cm, up to 1. 0 if the two arms ever touch, or if the hammer ever touches the controlled arm; the run stops at the first such contact.
reset_notes: Put the nail back on its rack, the hammer back on its face and rest, and push the nail's resistance in the post back to the top of the hole.
fidelity: Approximate. The wood's grip on the nail is a 20 N friction plug under the point; a nail not yet 1 cm in falls over unless held. Arm links collide as fitted capsules slightly larger than the real ones, so a near miss under about 1 cm can count as a touch. The gripper pinches with up to 50 N through flat pads. The controller uses the manufacturer's joint gains, gravity compensation and motor torque-speed limits. The other arm is scripted on the true scene state.
